# Pending changes (since patch 0024, 2026-11-26)
- (2026-11-26, the mesh editor fast again) Reported: everything slow. The mesh editor's interface update
  refreshes the Curve modeling panel, and the overview's "has anything changed" check serialized every
  solid's whole recipe - a baked solid's includes its mesh, edge points and curves as made (thousands of
  numbers) - ~15 ms each time, a refresh ~28 ms, many times a second (frames of 65-71 ms). The check now
  hashes a brief of each recipe (`_spec_brief`: steps, kinds, curve ids - not mesh / fv / c0 / chains):
  a panel refresh 28 -> 1 ms, the editor's interface update 18 -> 0.5 ms; frames back to the vsync's
  16.7 ms. File: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (_tree_sig, _spec_brief).
- (2026-11-26, dragging a baked solid's point fast again) Reported: moving a curve point still very slow,
  topology a mess. On the user's solid (grown to 14.9k triangles - each settle's loop cuts added rows that
  never went) a drag frame took ~530 ms: normals 162 ms (text-keyed lookups), untangling 140, flip fixes
  55, the solve's per-frame set-up ~100 (text keys), the wireframe rebuilt every frame ~98. Now: loop cuts
  off at settling (the mesh no longer grows); untangling and flip fixes only when the drag is let go;
  shading per corner from a once-per-mesh corner table (`EdgeNet.corner_topo` / `shaded_fast`); the
  solve's column lookups precomputed in `cg_setup` (flat arrays), 8 rounds + 1 smoothing pass while
  dragging (warm-started), the full solve on release; the wireframe hidden during a drag and drawn again
  after. A frame on that 14.9k mesh: ~530 -> ~100 ms (a fresh bake's ~3.5k: a quarter of that). Files:
  scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (corner_topo, shaded_fast, cg_setup, cg_moves),
  scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (_edge_mesh, settle_edges), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd
  (update_wire), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (the folding test checks the shape after release).
  The user's solid re-baked (asked): their original solids baked again and every edge's shape put back
  by its name as one step - 14.9k -> 3.8k triangles, closed, 88% in quads; a drag frame ~28 ms.
- (2026-11-26, every edit bent from the bake) Reported: the topology distorted again after another edit.
  Each settle made the settled mesh the solid's new start, so edits piled up (a second edit bent the
  first edit's rebuilt faces, their columns no longer along the solid's way up - crumpled triangles). Now
  a baked solid keeps its bake (spec "orig": the mesh, edge points and curves as baked, kept at the first
  settle): while its curves differ from the settled shape (a drag) it's bent from the bake with all the
  edits at once (`_orig_view`, `_edges_moved`), and settling starts from that too - so any number of
  edits gives what applying them all at once to the bake gives. Checked: the user's bake, their edits,
  then their next move - clean, closed, 3768 triangles throughout. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd
  (_orig_view, _edges_moved, _edge_mesh, settle_edges).
- (2026-11-26, settling fits the mesh's edges to their curves) Asked: higher resolution so the mesh fills
  the curve outline. A reshaped curve stretched the bake's edge points apart - straight segments cutting
  inside it. Settling now finds every mesh edge along a reshaped curve whose middle strays more than
  ~4% of the grid step (at least 1.5 mm) from the curve (`EdgeNet._off_curve`) and splits it with a loop
  cut through its quads (`_split_bent` seeded with those edges - quads kept, the new point on the curve),
  up to three rounds. From the bake each time, so it never accumulates. The user's solid: 3768 -> 4568
  triangles, closed, its outline on its curves. File: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd.
- (2026-11-26, settling clears slivers) Reported (zoomed in): a shading and topology issue at the corner of
  the reshaped recess. Settling left near-coincident points (a loop cut's new point beside an existing one)
  and fans of thin triangles along the rims. Now `EdgeNet.tidy_mesh` ends each settle: points closer than
  12% of the grid step merged (an edge or corner point kept over an inner one; a curve's point only into one
  on the same curves; never turning a triangle over), then thin triangles (smallest angle under 15°)
  lying nearly flat beside a neighbour turned to their best by edge flips - never across the solid's edges
  (neighbouring points of one curve, or faces meeting over 45°); kept only if the mesh stays closed. The
  user's solid (re-baked): long thin triangles 250 -> 28, 4356 triangles, closed, shading within 30°.
  Left: where a face narrows to a sharp corner (the recess's side meeting its top arc at an acute angle)
  its rows converge to that point. File: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (tidy_mesh, settle).
- (2026-11-26, the corner where two reshaped edges meet) Reported: the same shading problem where the two
  curves meet. The recess's side face had a crease beside its bent edge (its first row pulled with the
  edge, the next not) and crumpled points at the sharp corner. `tidy_mesh` now also fairs the faces near
  reshaped edges (the inner points within 12 rings of them eased towards their neighbours' middle, 20
  rounds - each face shaped by its edges) and smooths crumples (inner points whose triangles face more
  than 30° apart eased, never folding); points merge within 20% of the grid step. The user's solid
  (re-baked): no crease along the edge, the face shading in one smooth gradient, 4292 triangles, closed.
  File: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (tidy_mesh, settle).
- (2026-11-26, points on the solid's edges held while smoothing) Reported: a mess on the top rim (a dent
  - a wall triangle poking into the top). A column's end that lay on the cylinder's top rim but wasn't
  counted as one of the rim's points was eased off the rim by the fairing and crumple smoothing. Now
  `EdgeNet._on_edges` finds every point lying on a segment of the solid's edges (a spatial grid over the
  edges' segments) and `tidy_mesh` holds those as fixed too. The user's solid (re-baked): the rim clean,
  the corner still smooth, 4278 triangles, closed, shading within 30°. File: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd.
- (2026-11-26, cuts into a baked solid follow their curves) Reported: a new negative extrusion cut into the
  baked solid; moving its curve didn't change the solid. The cut made the part a live boolean ("baked
  solid minus the extrusion"), but `solid_of` couldn't build a baked side (kind "edges" needs its part's
  cache) - it returned nothing, so the part was never made again. Now `solid_of(spec, p)` builds a baked
  side through `edge_solid` with the part (found by its net when not given - `_holds_spec`), and a
  boolean's key is made of each side's own key (a baked side's brief, not its whole mesh). Moving the
  circle: the hole follows (~150 ms a rebuild on the user's solid). Known: a baked solid inside a boolean
  doesn't settle after edits of its own edges yet. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (solid_of,
  _holds_spec, _solid_key, refresh_solids), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd
  (test_cut_into_baked_solid_follows_its_curve).
- (2026-11-26, the view turns round the selection) Asked: turning the view always round the selection -
  a solid, a curve or a point, the smallest taking priority. `_orbit_pivot` (worked out once a drag): the
  mesh points picked in edit mode, else the curve point last pressed while its curve is picked, else the
  picked curves' middle (`CurveTools.selection_centre`), else the selected solids' bounds' middle. Files:
  scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd
  (test_view_turns_round_the_selection), data/docs/editor.md.
- (2026-11-26, the mesh follows its curves after a cut is baked in) Reported: the topology didn't follow a
  curve (an arc of a solid baked again after a cut). Two faults: (1) baking a solid with a cut in it made a
  mesh with holes - the quad builder left 216 open edges on that shape (97 traced edges) and the later
  passes only partly closed them; now a bake whose quad mesh isn't closed uses the even remesh (closed),
  and the flat faces' quads are kept only if the mesh stays closed; (2) settling's column straightening
  piled an arc's points at its two ends (each moved towards its partner across a shorter edge, kept 0.2%
  apart) - leaving the arc's middle with long straight segments; now the points of a run stay at least
  half an even share apart (clamped forward then back). The user's solid (their latest bake redone, their
  63 edges' shapes put back): closed, the arc's points spread evenly along it, shading within 30°.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (bake_edges, _edge_mesh's caps pass),
  scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (straighten_columns).
- (2026-11-26, one curve an edge) Reported: too many small curves next to each other - should be one curve
  with points along that edge. Tracing split an edge at every junction (a point where a third sharp edge
  meets it - on a baked solid baked again, the creases of its curved walls), e.g. a recess's outline in a
  dozen pieces. Now at a junction the two edges carrying on from each other (within 45° of straight on,
  the straightest pairs first) are one edge running through it (`EdgeNet.trace` / `_walk` "through"),
  the junction a point on it; and an edge bending gently through its points becomes a path curve (smooth
  there, sharp only where it turns over 30°), not a polyline. The user's solid (re-baked, their reshaped
  edges carried over by matching ends): 63 -> 42 curves, the recess outline one path of 10 points; closed.
  File: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (trace, _walk, chain_curve).
- (2026-11-26, baking checks its curves: joined, merged, lean) Asked: no unnecessary curves that could be
  one, no curves with too many points - checked on every bake. Tracing now: drops loose ends (a run of
  sharp edges dying out on a surface, again till none), merges two edges meeting end to end where nothing
  else meets (`EdgeNet.tidy_chains`), and every point two edges share is kept on each (`must` - the curves
  stay joined; an edge with such a point inside is a path, not a line / arc / circle). Paths get as few
  points as keep them on the edge (`fit_points`: ends, shared points and corners - turns over 30° in a
  step, sharp - then one at a time the point the smooth path strays furthest from, till within 0.4% of
  the edge's size). The user's solid (re-baked, their 3 reshaped edges carried over): 63 -> 41 curves, no
  loose ends, no edges meeting only each other, the longest 9 points (was 23); closed. Test:
  test_bake_makes_lean_joined_curves (a block baked, cut, baked again: no loose ends, no mergeable pairs,
  <= 24 curves, <= 16 points on one). Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (trace, tidy_chains,
  chain_curve, fit_points, _lean), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (bake_edges), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, a boolean's kinked seams one edge) Reported: still edges that shouldn't be separate - where a
  boolean (a cut) met a wall, its seam kinked at each junction, so a ledge round the solid came out as
  several curves (e.g. an arc of the cut between two arcs of the wall). Tracing now carries an edge on
  through a junction when it bends up to 80° there (was 45°; a box's 90° corners still end their edges),
  judged a few steps along each run (`_away` - a seam can kink at its first step); the kink a sharp point
  of the one curve. The user's solid (re-baked): 41 -> 32 curves, the ledge one path through the cut;
  closed, 4056 triangles. One of their three reshaped edges merged into a longer curve (its shape not
  carried over). File: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (trace, _away).
- (2026-11-26, a far pull no longer folds the mesh) Reported: geometry still easy to distort when a point is
  pulled far. Cause: an edge point's place along its curve was a fraction of the whole curve's length, so
  pulling one stretch of a long joined edge (a rim, down a side, along the bottom - one curve) slid the
  points on its other stretches along it, past its corners - triangles turned over (the user's solid: 23
  folds inside faces, up to 180°). Now places carry over span by span between the curve's points
  (`EdgeNet.span_map` / `map_t`: the same fraction within the same stretch; the plain fraction when points
  were added or taken) - in the drag (`edge_moves`) and on letting go (settle_edges maps the edge points'
  places before straightening). Settling hardened too: fairing never turns a triangle over or further round
  from how it faces (and eases one already turned over back), merges keep the mesh whole (the link
  condition: no edge left with three triangles), turns never onto an edge that's already there, and a
  loop cut that would crowd an edge is undone. The user's solid settled again: 23 -> 0 folds, closed, no
  crowded edges, 4130 triangles (85% in quads). Test: test_far_pull_keeps_edge_points_in_their_spans.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (span_map, map_t, edge_moves, tidy_mesh, settle, _crowded_edges,
  _tn, corner_edges), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd
  (settle_edges), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-26, points, patches, menu-only tools, grouped icons, quads) Asked: clicking a point picks and
  highlights it; pick several and separate them into a new curve without changing the geometry (still
  shaping it); merge curves by merging two of their points; mesh-editing-like tools (extrude...); pick a
  patch (the area a few curves bound), move it and set its resolution; every icon the right-click menu has
  removed from everywhere else; icons of one kind as one icon (click: the default, held: a drop-down of the
  others); the right-click menu didn't fold as it opened; topology with consistent subdivisions, quads, few
  lone triangles. Done:
  - Points: a click on a picked curve's point picks it (orange, bigger, ringed), Shift+click more; a drag
    moves all the picked points; G / R / S move / turn / scale them about their middle. New tools (the
    menu's Points group): Separate (Y) - a run of picked points its own curve, the rest the curves either
    side, nothing moves; on a baked solid its edge chain split the same way (EdgeNet.split_chain: each edge
    point put on its piece at its place within it), mesh untouched, each piece still shapes it. Merge (M) -
    two curve ends: one curve (a corner where they met), both ends of one curve: closed; a baked solid's
    chains joined (EdgeNet.merge_chains); other points welded at their middle. Extrude (E) - an open
    curve's end grows a new point that follows the mouse (click keeps, right-click takes back); from any
    other point a new line. Subdivide, Connect (F), Delete points (X). A baked solid touched is rebased
    first (its settled mesh its new start) so places carry over point by point.
  - Patches: a click on a baked solid's face (Curve modeling tab) picks it - the face between its edges
    (flooded between chain edges and real corners), shaded orange, its edges' curves picked; G / R / S
    move / turn / scale its every point (joined edges follow at shared corners), the mesh settles. Patch
    resolution (panel spin 0-3, or Patch finer / coarser in the menu): each step cuts every quad of the
    patch in four with loop cuts carried on through the quads beyond (quads kept, closed); coarser restores
    the mesh from before (kept in the spec's res_stack) bent to the edges as they are.
  - Menu-only tools: hide_menu_twins hides every toolbar / side-panel / header icon button whose icon a
    right-click menu tool has (the mode, select kinds, knife, views, gizmo, move modes, proportional, symmetry,
    primitives, edit-mesh, booleans, mirror Apply, the curve panel's sketch / edit / solid / mesh rows, save,
    undo, redo) - they still work (keys, state). The curve panel's "On the mesh" section gone.
  - Grouped icons: scripts/ui/icon_group.gd - one icon for a group: click runs the default (last picked),
    a held press (0.32 s) or right-click drops the others down; a corner mark. The right-click menu's tools
    grouped by kind (MENU_FAMILIES: move/turn/scale, views, frame, undo/redo, select kinds, select all/none/
    invert/loop/ring, deform, add primitives, booleans, mirror, bind, symmetry, proportional, normals,
    remove, cut, faces; the curve page: sketch, planes, transforms, copies, offset/fillet, join/bridge,
    curve booleans, solids, mesh tools, point kinds, points, patch), the page one flowing row of group
    icons (the Curve modeling page: 40 icons -> 13). The header: New / Import / Save as one icon, the
    variants (add / duplicate / erase) one.
  - The menu's fold on opening: a window can't be drawn smaller than its contents, so a stand-in panel
    unrolls from the top (0.5 s) while the menu's own panel is see-through and its icons scale open and
    fade in; closing hides it and the stand-in rolls up (as before). Lambdas hold no freed nodes (ids).
  - Quads: EdgeNet.pair_quads - two side-by-side lone triangles (neither half of a quad) whose shared side
    turned to the other diagonal makes it the longest side of both (a convex, flat quad, not across an
    edge) are turned; run once when a baked mesh is first drawn (spec flag "paired") and in every settle
    (tidy_mesh). The user's solid: lone triangles 596 -> 286 (14% -> 7% of 4130), closed, no folds.
  Tests: test_points_pick_separate_merge, test_points_extrude_connect_delete_and_move,
  test_patch_pick_move_and_resolution, test_menu_groups_fold_and_no_twins. Docs: editor.md (mesh-curves:
  menu tools and grouped icons; new sections mesh-curves-points, mesh-curves-patches).
  Files: scripts/ui/icon_group.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (menu: mesh_menu_groups,
  MENU_FAMILIES, _menu_page, _menu_unroll / _unroll_step / _unroll_end, _menu_close; hide_menu_twins; header
  groups), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (points: picked_points, pick_point, separate_points,
  merge_points, extrude_points, subdivide_points, connect_points, delete_points, points_items, _xf_points;
  patches: picked_patch, _faces_of, _face_ids, _patch_tris, pick_patch, patch_finer / coarser, patch_level,
  set_patch_level, _patch_row, _draw_patch; drag of several points, grab mode; the paired pass),
  scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (split_chain, merge_chains, pair_quads), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_icons.gd
  (8 new icons), data/docs/editor.md, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.

- (2026-11-26, the picked patch / solid shaded with the scene) Reported: with a curve solid picked, areas
  showed overlaid on each other instead of hidden behind the solid. The shading was drawn flat over the
  view (every front-facing triangle, the solid's own hidden faces through it). Now it's a see-through orange
  skin in the 3D scene a hair outside the surface (StandardMaterial3D unshaded, alpha 0.3, grow ~0.2% of
  the solid's size), depth-tested - hidden wherever the solid hides it: the whole solid shares the part's
  mesh; a patch is a mesh of its triangles (where the part draws them now). Kept beside the model, not a
  part, never saved; rebuilt only when the patch or the part's mesh changes; freed with the curve tools.

- (2026-11-26, outline only round the shape; the picked solid's shading drawn) Reported: a selected solid
  showed occluded geometry over it. Two causes: (1) the 2D shading the layer drew stayed on screen after
  the code changed (the 3D skin replaced it; the view draws on request - the skin now asks for a redraw
  when it shows, hides or moves); (2) the selected part's outline (an inverted hull pushed out in screen
  space) also drew lines over the shape's own folds and holes. The outline is now two passes: the shape's

  shaders/outline.gdshader, scripts/editor/select_outline.gd, curve_tools.gd (_sync_pick_overlay).

- (2026-11-26, curve modeling at 120 FPS or more) Asked: heavy optimisation - curve modeling never under
  120 FPS. Measured on the user's solid (4.4k triangles, 34 curves, my window uncapped): orbiting 21.5 ms a
  frame -> 1.2-2.2 ms; dragging a point 61 ms per update (p95 89 ms) -> 1.8 ms median, 7.4 ms p95, 9 ms max;
  letting go 1.7 s frozen -> 1 ms on the release frame and ~6 ms when the settled mesh arrives; idle 0.8 ms.
  How: (1) curves drawn as 3D lines (shaders/curve_line.gdshader: screen-wide quads, a dark rim pass and the
  colour pass, tone mapping compensated) - the GPU's depth hides them behind solids, no ray per point; each
  curve's strip kept and only changed curves re-sampled; the picked curves' points still drawn flat, their
  occlusion skipped while dragging. (2) EdgeNet.edge_moves: unchanged curves skipped, each changed curve
  sampled once, places found by halving (35 ms -> 0.6 ms). (3) A drag's solve (8 CG rounds) and shading on a
  worker (_drag_job_start / take), the newest move waiting for the one being worked out; the drag's
  solver set up on the worker with the weights (cg_setup no longer on the first drag frame: 48 ms).
  (4) Letting go (point drags, group drags, G / R / S): settling split into _settle_inputs (main, ~1 ms),
  _settle_compute (worker: the edges' moves, the full solve, untangle, columns, settle, orient, weights,
  solver, shading, flat arrays) and _settle_apply (main), the undo step made when it lands
  (_changed_async / _settle_finish; a new press, undo, redo or save takes it first); programmatic edits
  (_changed) stay synchronous. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd,
  shaders/curve_line.gdshader (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (undo / redo / save), tests.

- (2026-11-26, conversion quality and speed) Asked: a safeguard so a conversion's result is high quality -
  no distorted geometry, shading issues, z-fighting or anything ugly - then the conversion as fast as it can be.
  Done: each solid's result is checked against what it was made from, on its worker (CurveTools._quality): its
  surface where the old one was, both ways (at most 2% of the piece's size off, 0.4% on average; nothing lost,
  3%), no triangles facing the wrong way (a thin shell's two walls allowed), no slivers it didn't have, no
  doubled triangles (z-fighting), no new holes, every corner's shading within 60 degrees of its face. A solid
  is now made on its own triangles first, exactly, its edges laid along them (_exact_mesh - nothing moved);
  one that falls short is made again untouched (no seams closed, no triangles paired); an even quad remesh
  only when its edges aren't on its points. Doubled triangles always taken out (_no_doubles); a remeshed open
  piece turned the way the old one faced (_faces_away). A smooth piece with no edges (an eye, a ball) gets a
  seam round its middle along its own mesh's edges (_seam_loops) - every piece of all 12 characters converts.
  Checked over all 12 characters (bench: 60-153 solids each): 0 errors, 0 failing the check.
  Speed: several solids made at once (all cores but two; CurveTools.convert_workers), started ~4 ms a frame;
  the check measures only what's new (an exact copy's own triangles recognised by their corners - 22 s ->
  3.7 s of worker time on the pirate); an exact copy skips the tying-in, the cap check and the second seam
  pass; the faces' reveal drawn by a shader number (no mesh rebuilt a frame); the store's meshes read a few a
  frame and its weights, meshes and JSON made on workers; the split's piece meshes made on its worker. The
  player: ~100 s -> ~10 s in the editor (1.2 s of work on 22 workers; the rest the reveal and the store).
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd.

- (2026-11-26, quads; a quick cancel) Asked: right-click cancel slow; the solid's topology all wrong, too many
  triangles - as many quads as possible in any solid, triangles only when unavoidable.
  Quads: a converted solid's triangles paired into quads (two lying flat together across their longest side,
  not across an edge of the solid), then split as a subdivision surface's first step without its smoothing (a
  point at each side's and each face's middle: a quad four quads, a lone triangle three) - every face a quad,
  the surface where it was; again while a side's over a quarter of the solid (up to 1,200 quads)
  (EdgeNet.quadify, _pair_faces, _faces_to_tris: each quad two triangles split along its longer diagonal, so
  it reads as one). New conversions are quads; solids converted before are made quads in the background,
  ~6 ms a frame (CurveTools._quads_step - an edited one made again from its bake in quads), only solids
  converted from a model (_from_model), not ones baked from recipes. A settle of a quad solid evens its
  points without turning diagonals (even_faces with no flips). The user's Upper R Red made again from its
  exact copy in the stored variant, in quads: 11,715 -> 1,004 triangles, 0 folds.
  Cancel: only the edges the drag moved put back and only their solids made again (it set the whole state
  back - all 91 of a character's solids remade). A recipe-baked solid's settle turns its triangles outwards
  as before (the converted solids' orientation from their bake only for those).
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd.
- (2026-11-26, ECurves at 30 FPS and more on a whole character) Asked: test ECurves modelling thoroughly and
  keep it from ever dropping under 30 FPS on the character being worked on (91 solids, ~144k triangles).
  Measured with a bench playing every action frame by frame on a copy of it (idle, orbit, zoom, hover, pick,
  drag a vertex / a face / a solid / the collection, let go, right-click cancel, undo, redo, G, overview,
  wireframe, knife) and the profiler. Before -> after (average / worst frame, ms): vertex drag 126/172 ->
  10/16, solid drag 195/385 -> 8/28, face drag + cancel 108/884 -> 9/34, collection pick 1,370 -> 28,
  first drag of a solid 1,650 -> no wait, knife 290 -> 45 (once), undo / redo 8 s (all solids remade) -> 2/4.
  What was slow and what changed (curve_tools.gd, edge_net.gd, mesh_editor.gd):
  * a drag frame done on a worker marked every solid stale - all 91 remade each frame: only its own;
  * moving a corner searched every solid and curve per point: an index made once a frame; a solid dragged
    whole is its settled mesh shifted on the worker, no solving; its corners not matched at all;
  * a drag's edge moves, its solve, its shading and the picked face's overlay all on the worker;
  * while dragging only the solids it can change are looked at, and only their edges' lines remade;
  * blend weights (a solid's first drag, or after undo) 1.5 s -> 0.2 s (tiny far weights skipped, no
    sorting), made on a worker - the drag goes on, the mesh follows when they're ready; a settle makes its
    own when they aren't; triangle grid for the settle's facing check sized by the mesh (seconds -> ms);
  * undo copies share meshes (only ever replaced) and are reused while a solid is unchanged; undo / redo
    and cancel remake only the solids that differ; a cancel puts back the mesh it had;
  * picking a collection selects its solids at once (ninety overview refills before); overview signature
    hashed; the overview filled the frame after a drag, a cancel or a knife cut;
  * guide levels, each solid's faces and the pick overlay made ahead while nothing's going on; a press on a
    face splits its work and the first move over two frames; a knife cut over three.
  Tests: all 327 pass; fps_test talos within baseline.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd, scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd.
